questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Instead of working on the
project, she does nothing but
to scroll through social media.
options_hi: Instead of working on the
project, she does nothing but
to scroll through social media.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “to scroll” with “scroll”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Bare Infinitives after "Do + Nothing + But"

This is a specific idiomatic construction in English. When the word "but" (or "except") is used in the sense of "excluding" or "other than," and it is preceded by a form of the verb "do" (do, does, did), the verb that follows must be a Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to").

Even if the sentence is in the past tense (using "did") or refers to a singular person (using "does"), the verb after "but" does not take "s," "ed," or "ing." It remains in its simplest, root form.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...she does nothing but to scroll through social media."

In this sentence, we have the trigger "does nothing but." The verb following "but" is "to scroll" (a full infinitive). According to the rule, the "to" must be removed. The verb should simply be "scroll."

Corrected Sentence

Instead of working on the project, she does nothing but scroll through social media.

options_en: Considering the rapidly deteriorating weather
conditions in the mountains, you
had better cancelled your trip.
options_hi: Considering the rapidly deteriorating weather
conditions in the mountains, you
had better cancelled your trip.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “cancelled” with “cancel”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Bare Infinitives after "Had better"

The phrase "Had better" is a modal idiom used to give strong advice or to indicate what is a desirable or necessary action in a specific situation. Regardless of the fact that it contains the word "had" (which usually signals the past tense), it refers to the present or future. It must always be followed by a Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to").

Using a Past Participle (V3), a Past Tense verb (V2), or a Full Infinitive (to + V1) after "had better" is a common grammatical error.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...you had better cancelled your trip."

In this sentence, "had better" is used to provide advice regarding the weather. The verb following "had better" is "cancelled" (the past participle form). According to the rule, this must be in the base form. Therefore, "cancelled" must be changed to "cancel".

REMEMBER: Use bare infinitives after these ; Had better/ Had rather / Would better/ Would rather

corrected Sentence

Considering the rapidly deteriorating weather conditions in the mountains, you had better cancel your trip.

📌 Rule / Concept: Perfect Modal in Passive Voice (Modal + have been + V³)

When an active sentence contains a perfect modal structure such as: Modal + have + V³

The passive form must follow the structure: Modal + have been + V³

The word “been” is compulsory in perfect modal passive constructions. The modal remains unchanged, the object becomes the subject, and the verb shifts to past participle (V³).

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

In perfect modal passive, “been” is mandatory. The structure is always “modal + have been + V³.” Never drop “been.” Do not change the modal meaning while converting.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The project manager is confident that the
engineering team will have completed the bridge
by the time the monsoon season will begin in July.
options_hi: The project manager is confident that the
engineering team will have completed the bridge
by the time the monsoon season will begin in July.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “will begin” with “begins”

📌 Rule / Concept: Future Perfect Tense and Time Clauses

Future perfect + ‘by the time’ + present indefinite

When describing an action that will be completed by a certain point in the future, we use the Future Perfect Tense (will + have + V3).

The most critical part of this rule for competitive exams is the Time Clause (the part of the sentence starting with by the time, when, or before). Even though the entire sentence refers to the future, the time clause must be in the Simple Present Tense (V1 / V{s/es}). Using "will" in both parts of the sentence is a grammatical error known as a "double future" trap.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...the engineering team will have completed the bridge by the time the monsoon season will begin..."

In this sentence:

  1. The completion of the bridge (First future action) is correctly in the Future Perfect (will + have + V3).

  2. The arrival of the monsoon (The time-marker/deadline) is introduced by "by the time."

According to the rule of conditional and time clauses, you cannot use "will" after "by the time." The future intent is already established in the main clause, so the time clause must revert to the Simple Present.

Corrected Sentence

The project manager is confident that the engineering team will have completed the bridge by the time the monsoon season begins in July.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: By the time you reach the station, the train will have left.

Example 2 ✅: I will have finished this report before the manager calls me.

Example 3 ✅: By the time she returns, we will have prepared the dinner.

📌 Rule / Concept: “Unless” = If Not (No Double Negative)

“Unless” already carries a negative meaning.
It means “if not.”

Structure: Unless + Subject + Verb (affirmative form), main clause

We must NOT use “not” in the clause introduced by “unless” because that creates a double negative.

💢 Application to the Given Question - “Unless” already means “if not”. So the sentence actually becomes:

If the candidates do not do not submit…

This is grammatically incorrect.

Correct structure: Unless the candidates submit the requisite category certificates…

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ - Unless you pay the fee, your registration will be cancelled.

Example 2 ✅- Unless the bank verifies the documents, the loan will not be sanctioned.

Example 3 ✅ - Unless the report is submitted on time, disciplinary action will follow.

the crisis prevented large-scale administrative failure.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D).

There is no error in the above question.

Rule / Concept: Use of “THE” before Superlative Degree.

A superlative degree expresses the highest or extreme degree of a quality within a defined group. Since it is specific and unique, it must be preceded by the definite article “the”.

Application to the Given Question -

“The committee unanimously agreed that the most effective strategy adopted during the crisis prevented large-scale administrative failure.”

Here, “most effective” is a superlative degree referring to one specific strategy out of all possible strategies adopted during the crisis so “The” is correctly used.

More Examples for Clarity -

She delivered the best performance in the final round.

This is the most reliable source of information available.

He faced the toughest challenge of his career.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Superlative degree → “the” is compulsory

Look for words like best, worst, most, least, finest, gravest.

Absence of “the” before superlative is a sure-shot error.

Rule / Concept: The Noun "Headquarters"

Headquarters is a unique noun in English that always ends in -s, whether it is used in a singular or plural context. The form "headquarter" (without the 's') as a noun is technically incorrect in standard English; it only exists as a verb (e.g., "to headquarter a company").

Key Usage Points:

-Singular: The headquarters is...

-Plural: The various headquarters are...

-Form: It never drops the 's' when functioning as a noun.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the word "various" indicates that the speaker is referring to more than one main office location (plural). As established, the word remains "headquarters." Because it is plural in this context, the verb "are" is correctly used. The sentence maintains both the correct noun form and correct subject-verb agreement.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 - The company's headquarters is located in London. (Singular use)

Example 2 - All regional headquarters were notified of the change. (Plural use)

Example 3 - A new headquarters was built last year. (Even with 'A', the 's' remains)

Incorrect Usage:

Wrong example 1 - The headquarter of the UN is in New York. ❌

Wrong example 2 - He visited the army headquarter yesterday. ❌

questions.q_en:
Ethical conduct in public and private life is often tested not during moments of convenience but in situations that demand personal sacrifice. While individuals may profess strong moral beliefs, real commitment becomes evident when actions involve [--1---] consequences rather than symbolic gestures. In professional environments, ethical lapses are frequently justified as pragmatic compromises, yet such reasoning can gradually [-----2----] moral accountability. Over time, repeated rationalization of minor transgressions fosters a climate of [----3---] indifference, where wrongdoing is normalized rather than questioned. Scholars therefore argue that ethical integrity must be sustained through a [---4----] adherence to values, independent of external reward or recognition.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [2] :

• Institutionalize suggests formal adoption, not erosion.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Adjective Triggers)

The Present Subjunctive mood is not only triggered by verbs but also by specific adjectives that express necessity, urgency, or importance (such as vital, essential, imperative, important, mandatory). When these adjectives are followed by a "that-clause," the verb in that clause must remain in its base form, regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The adjective vital functions as the trigger here. The subject of the following clause is "every high-ranking official." In standard indicative English, you would use "undergoes" (singular verb for a singular subject). However, because of the subjunctive trigger (vital), the verb must shift to its base form: undergo.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ It is vital that he be informed of the changes.

Example 2 ✅ It is essential that the witness tell the truth. (Not tells)

Example 3 ✅ It is important that she not forget the password.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • Spot the Adjective: Train your eyes to catch "It is [Adjective] that..." structures. Common culprits: Vital, Essential, Imperative, Crucial.

  • The S-Ending Trap: This is the most effective way examiners hide errors in long sentences. They know "official undergoes" sounds natural to the untrained ear.

  • if I were disciplined
  • under different circumstances

Hence, should stands on its own and is grammatically complete.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The environmental organization worked tirelessly
to protect the wetlands since the new
industrial policy was proposed last year.
options_hi: The environmental organization worked tirelessly
to protect the wetlands since the new
industrial policy was proposed last year.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “worked” with “has been working”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Perfect Continuous with 'Since'

When an action starts at a specific point in the past and continues up to the present moment, we must use the Present Perfect Continuous

The word "Since" is a major indicator of this tense. It marks the starting point of the action.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"The environmental organization worked... since the new industrial policy was proposed..."

  1. The Starting Point: The policy was proposed (Simple Past - V2).

  2. The Ongoing Action: The organization's work started then and is still happening because the sentence uses "since."

  3. The Error: By using "worked," the sentence implies the organization stopped working. Since the effort is ongoing in response to the policy, it must be "has been working."



Corrected Sentence

The environmental organization has been working tirelessly to protect the wetlands since the new industrial policy was proposed last year.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The quality of the mangoes
imported from the tropical
islands are excellent.
No Error.
options_hi: The quality of the mangoes
imported from the tropical
islands are excellent.
No Error.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C)- The plural verb "are" must be replaced with the singular verb "is."

Rule/Concept: Subject vs. Subject Qualifier: The verb must always agree with the main subject, not the nouns found in the qualifying phrases (the sub-qualifiers). In this sentence, the verb should agree with "The quality," which is a singular uncountable noun.

Logic Breakdown:

The Main Subject: The sentence is not describing the mangoes themselves, but rather "The quality" of those mangoes.

The Qualifier: "of the mangoes imported from the tropical islands" is a prepositional phrase acting as a qualifier. It provides extra detail but does not change the number of the subject.

The Distractor: The word "islands" or "mangoes" is plural and sits right before the verb to trick the student into picking "are".

Agreement: Since "Quality" is singular, the verb must be the singular form "is".

Correct Sentence: The quality of the mangoes imported from the tropical islands is excellent.
